claim: Uganda's Ministry of Health confirmed three new Ebola cases on 23 May 2026, raising the country's total confirmed infections to five
summary: In a press statement signed by Director General Health Services Prof. Charles Olaro, Uganda's Ministry of Health confirmed three new Ebola Virus Disease cases on 23 May 2026 — two Ugandans (a driver and a health worker linked to the country's first patient) and a Congolese woman who had travelled from Arua to Entebbe — bringing confirmed infections to five.

citations.title: Uganda confirms three new Ebola cases

claim: Uganda's Ministry of Health declared the 2026 Ebola outbreak over in late July 2026, after 20 confirmed cases
summary: Uganda's Ministry of Health declared the 2026 Ebola outbreak over after a 42-day monitoring period following the last confirmed patient's discharge on 16 June 2026. The outbreak totalled 20 confirmed cases, with 18 patients recovering.

citations.title: Ebola Update: Uganda Declares End of 2026 Ebola Outbreak

claim: Uganda's Electoral Commission declared Yoweri Museveni the winner of the January 2026 presidential election, with about 71.6% of the vote
summary: The Electoral Commission announced on 17 January 2026, two days after voting, that President Yoweri Museveni had won a seventh term with about 71.6% of the vote. His main challenger, Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu (Bobi Wine), received about 24.7%; the opposition rejected the result as neither free nor fair.

citations.title: Museveni Declared Winner of Uganda's Presidential Election Amid Opposition Rejection

claim: Yoweri Museveni was sworn in for a seventh presidential term on 12 May 2026 at Kololo Independence Grounds
summary: Museveni was sworn in for his seventh presidential term on 12 May 2026 at Kololo Independence Grounds. A new cabinet for the 2026-2031 term, retaining Janet Museveni as Minister of Education and Sports and Peter Ogwang as State Minister for Sports, was announced two weeks later via the President's official account.

citations.title: First Lady Janet Museveni, Peter Ogwang Keep Sports Docket in New Cabinet

claim: Uganda's annual headline inflation rose to 4.0% in July 2026, up from 3.7% in June
summary: The Bank of Uganda's August 2026 Monetary Policy Statement, reported by the Daily Monitor, put annual headline inflation at 4.0% in July 2026, up from 3.7% in June, driven mainly by higher energy, fuel and food-crop prices.

citations.title: Bank of Uganda holds benchmark rate at 9.75% as inflation edge prompts caution

claim: The Bank of Uganda held its Central Bank Rate at 9.75% on 13 August 2026
summary: Governor Michael Atingi-Ego announced on 13 August 2026 that the Monetary Policy Committee had kept the Central Bank Rate at 9.75%, while projecting headline inflation of 5.5% to 6.0% over the following 12 months.

citations.title: Bank of Uganda holds benchmark rate at 9.75% as inflation edge prompts caution

claim: Uganda's Communications Commission ordered a nationwide shutdown of public internet access starting 6pm on 13 January 2026, ahead of the presidential election
summary: A UCC directive dated 13 January 2026 and signed by Executive Director Nyombi Thembo ordered telecom operators to suspend public internet access and selected mobile services from 6pm that day, and to halt new SIM registrations, exempting healthcare, banking, government and security systems.

citations.title: Uganda Communications Commission (UCC) Orders Temporary Internet Shutdown Ahead of 2026 Presidential Election

claim: Starlink disabled its satellite internet service in Uganda effective 1 January 2026, after a UCC directive over unlicensed operation
summary: Following a Uganda Communications Commission directive on unlicensed satellite service, Starlink (Space Exploration Technologies Corp.) restricted its terminals in Uganda effective 1 January 2026, confirmed in a letter from its Director of Market Access to the UCC's Executive Director dated 2 January 2026.

citations.title: Starlink Shuts Down Satellite Internet Services in Uganda Following Regulatory Directive

claim: Uganda signed a civil-works contract with Japan's Zenitaka Corporation on 10 July 2026 to build a new Karuma Bridge
summary: Uganda's Commissioner for National Roads, Isaac Wani, and Zenitaka Corporation's Osamu Tanabe signed the civil-works contract in Tokyo on 10 July 2026. Japan is funding about $32.7 million through its ODA programme, implemented by JICA, with construction due to start in October 2026 and take four years.

citations.title: Uganda secures funding for new Karuma Bridge

claim: Uganda's coffee sector recorded its best year on record between May 2024 and April 2025, exporting 7.17 million 60-kg bags worth $1.97 billion
summary: Uganda's Ministry of Agriculture Coffee Development Department reported that coffee exports in the year to April 2025 reached 7.17 million 60-kg bags earning $1.97 billion, up 21.7% in volume and about 95% in value from the previous year's 5.90 million bags worth $1.01 billion.

citations.title: Uganda coffee exports hit record high with nearly US$2B earned in 12 months

claim: Uganda's UNEB scheduled the release of 2025 UACE (A-Level) results for 13 March 2026 at a State House Nakasero ceremony
summary: UNEB scheduled the release of 2025 UACE results for 13 March 2026 at 11:00 AM at State House Nakasero, to be announced by Minister of Education and Sports Janet Museveni.
